bib.title: Large-Scale Hypothesis Testing and False-Discovery Rates (Chapter 15, Computer Age Statistical Inference)

question: How should one decide which of thousands of simultaneous null hypotheses to reject, and how does false-discovery-rate theory answer this compared with FWER control?
contributions: Introduces Bonferroni/Holm FWER control, Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control, the two-groups empirical Bayes model, local fdr, empirical/permutation nulls and relevance.

limits: Text layer drops minus signs: any negative value (e.g. Phi^-1(0.05/N)=-4.31, left cutoff -3.40, DTI delta0=-0.12) is sign unconfirmed except where the figure axis labels show it.
BH theorem requires independent null p-values; under correlation fdr-hat stays nearly unbiased but its variance grows (Notes 6).
Estimating the null adds variability to fdr-hat; stick with theoretical null when it looks right (prostate).
Authors call the survey of twenty-first-century topics 'more illustrative than definitive'.
practices: Control FDR at q=0.1 (usual) rather than FWER when N is in the thousands and most cases are null (p.276).
Report local fdr-hat<=0.2 as the interesting cutoff, matching Fdr-hat<=0.1 (p.285-286).
Check the z-value histogram centre against N(0,1); if too wide, estimate an empirical null (locfdr) (p.286-289).
Use a permutation null to fix asymptotic inaccuracy only; it cannot fix correlation, unobserved covariates or effect-size issues (p.290).
Decide which cases are relevant comparators before pooling (DTI example, p.291-293).
Estimate pairwise correlation alpha to judge whether correlation threatens the analysis (p.295-296).
In large-scale testing the usual goal is to accept most nulls, not reject (Summary p.293).

terms.definition: the probability of making even one false rejection, Pr{reject any true H0i} (15.7)
a/R, false rejections over total rejections, defined 0 if R=0; unobservable (15.11)
E{Fdp(D)}; rule D controls FDR at level q if FDR(D)<=q (15.12-15.13)
reject H0(i) for i<=imax, the largest i with p(i)<=(i/N)q (15.14); FDR = pi0*q <= q if nulls independent
each case is null with probability pi0 (density f0) or non-null with pi1=1-pi0 (density f1); mixture f=pi0 f0+pi1 f1 (15.19-15.22)
Pr{case i is null | zi >= z0} = pi0 S0(z0)/S(z0) (15.24)
Pr{case i is null | zi = z0} = pi0 f0(z)/f(z) (15.34, 15.38)
normal null N(delta0, sigma0^2) estimated from the central z-values by maximum likelihood (locfdr) instead of the theoretical N(0,1) (15.48)
histogram of z-values after randomly permuting group labels, suppressing real differences
q = N p_i / i, the q putting a case exactly on the rejection boundary
